title: Scheduler & Cadences
markdown:
The scheduler is an asyncio task started in the FastAPI lifespan (`openexecutive.scheduler.runner.run_scheduler`). It polls every 30s and reads due rows from `scheduled_actions` (in `episodic_memory.db`). The due query uses `claim_due_actions`, an UPDATE…RETURNING claim, so each row fires at most once per process — this assumes a single scheduler instance per database. Each due row runs in its own task, started with no audit scope (`audit.context.unscoped_audit_rows`): a scheduled action is unattended and never part of the turn that scheduled it, so its audit rows follow the ordinary rule. Polls are gated on an active company profile via `_company_profile_active()`; before onboarding, due rows stay `pending`.

### Operator pause

A global pause switch (`openexecutive.scheduler.pause`, one row in the `executive_control` table) stops everything the Executive starts on its own. It is the first check of every scheduler tick: while paused the tick does nothing — no alert/watchlist sweep, no claim — so due rows stay `pending` and fire on the first tick after resume. Actions already claimed when the pause lands run to completion; pausing holds work, it never cancels it. The same check gates the Gmail poller (the inbox is left unread) and the workflow resumer (no `wait_for_human` timeouts or resumes, and `apply_resolution` records a reply without kicking the run). Inbound conversations — web chat, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Google Chat — are deliberately not gated. The switch is set from the sidebar, the paused banner or Settings in the UI, or via `POST /executive/pause` / `POST /executive/resume`; each flip writes an `executive_paused` / `executive_resumed` audit row. Any signed-in caller may pause (it only holds work); resuming releases every held action at once, so it is the principal's alone (open only while no principal is on the roster). The state persists across restarts (boot logs a warning while paused) and across client-slot switches. `is_paused()` is read-only: a DB file or table that does not exist yet reads as "running", but a read error on an existing DB reads as "paused" — the brake fails closed, so a storage fault holds work rather than silently releasing it while the UI still shows "paused" (the UI shows "status unknown" when it cannot read the state).

### Liveness heartbeat

Every tick ends by recording when it finished and what it did — `ran`, `paused`, `waiting_for_company`, `rotating`, or `failed` when the tick raised — and `run_scheduler` notes when it started. `scheduler_heartbeat()` returns both; they live in process memory, not the database. Settings → Setup status (`GET /setup/status`) reads them: no start means the task isn't running; no tick five minutes after starting, or none for three poll intervals (at least 90 s), means the loop has stopped; `failed` and `waiting_for_company` get their own light. Liveness is judged before the pause switch, because a paused scheduler still ticks: one that has stopped shows as stopped, where the Resume button wouldn't help. A restart clears the previous run's last tick. Due actions run as their own tasks, so a slow brief never ages the heartbeat.

### A teammate's scheduled rows

`schedule_followup` and `suggest_workflow` keep the speaker on the row (`scheduled_actions.created_by_person_id`, from `Session.caller_person_id`). A due row whose creator is the principal, or that has no creator (the system's own rows, rows from before the column), takes the ordinary dispatch. A row a teammate queued runs as that teammate (`runner._run_teammate_followup`), because its intent is their own text: it is cancelled unless the creator is still an active team member and the row's address is one of their own; the Executive only writes the message, on an unattended session with `run_for_person_id` naming the teammate, which makes it read-only like a turn from another AI app that may not act (`schedule_tools.read_only_turn`: none of `MCP_CLIENT_WITHHELD_TOOLS` and only the gateway reads in `MCP_CLIENT_MCP_TOOLS`); its context is the decisions and advice of the conversation that queued it (nothing when there is none), never the company-wide list; and the runner sends the text to the teammate's own address on the row's channel (`_send_on_plan`), retrying on a failed send. A fork that limits what a teammate's turns may use applies the same limit to the run through `run_for_person_id`.

**A follow-up overtaken by events.** An ad hoc follow-up back to the person who set it (the row's creator, else its conversation's owner, the principal when it has none; and only when its address is their own, `runner._followup_owner`) fires with what they wrote in chat since it was set: up to 30 of their own messages, 300 characters each, across all their conversations (`session_store.own_messages_since`; only their words, never a reply or someone else's line), in `<since_scheduled>` tags as data. The run is asked first whether that shows it is already done or no longer needed, and if so to send nothing and answer `ALREADY_HANDLED: <why>`. The runner then records the row `cancelled` with `skipped: already handled (<why>)` and a `scheduled_action` audit row with phase `skipped`, instead of `done`. A teammate's row gets the same block and check before the runner sends what it wrote. A follow-up to anyone else, or with no chat since, fires exactly as before.

### Cadence DSL

`openexecutive.departments.cadence` supports, all in UTC for department and workflow cadences:

- `daily@HH:MM`
- `weekly@DOW@HH:MM` or `weekly@DOW-HH:MM` (DOW is a 3-letter day, e.g. `weekly@thu@09:00`)
- `quarterly@DD-HH:MM`

`PATCH /departments/{slug}` rejects a spec that does not parse (bad format, unknown DOW, out-of-range time) with a 422 naming the valid formats, so a typo is caught at save time instead of silently never firing. An empty spec means no cadence (the department page's **Off**). A new department starts weekly, `weekly@mon@09:00`. Changing a department's `check_in` through that route re-times it at once: `cadence.reschedule_check_in()` cancels its pending `dept_cadence` row and queues the next occurrence of the new spec (nothing when it is off or in solo); a check-in already running finishes, and its chain adds nothing because the new row is pending.

When a department cadence is due, the runner invokes the `department_check_in` workflow and chains the following occurrence via `cadence.enqueue_next()`. The fire is not passed through the authority gate: the check-in sends nothing (it grades Goals, writes one audit row and a Honcho note), and every action it proposes carries its own `gate_action` verdict in the report. Before creating a run the runner applies a skip rule (`department_check_in.needs_check_in`): the check-in is skipped when the department has no specialist agent, has no Goals, or nothing is new since its Goals were last reviewed — no decision or audit row tagged to the department (the check-in's own review row aside) since the oldest Goal's `last_reviewed_at`, and no Goal edited after it was graded. A Goal never reviewed always runs it. A skip leaves no run in the activity rail, is recorded as `cancelled` with its reason (`skipped: …` in `last_error`) rather than `done` — a done cadence row means "the check-in ran" to the nudge engine — and still chains the next occurrence; so does a check-in that fails once its retries are spent, so one broken department does not fall out of its cycle. That final failure also files one Home card, "*Finance* check-in didn't finish" (`workflows.failure_alerts`, source `workflow_failed`, tagged `failed_run:<run id>`; repeats of the same check-in coalesce into it), because nobody watches a scheduled run; a scheduled saved workflow (`dynamic_workflow`) that fails files the same card, routed to the person it delivers to. The card's **Run again** (`POST /workflows/runs/{run_id}/rerun`) queues the same action, due now, with `scope_key` `rerun:<run id>`: it skips the skip rule and does not chain another occurrence, and re-timing the check-in leaves it queued (the dept chain is idempotent anyway; a saved workflow's `schedule_dynamic_workflow_cadence` is skipped). Chaining is idempotent: while a next occurrence for the department is already pending nothing is added, so a row that chained and then failed to record its outcome never leaves two. Seeded departments start with no Goals, so their weekly check-ins cost nothing until someone adds one. Goals no check-in grades (no department, or a department with no specialist) are graded by the recurring `goal_review` kind instead (`GOAL_REVIEW_TIME`, default `weekly@mon@09:00` in the user's zone, both modes), seeded with the principal's rhythm and chained like the reflection: it runs `departments.goal_review.run_review` under `unscoped_audit_rows()`, delivers nothing, and a failed week never breaks the chain. Deleting a department cancels its pending `dept_cadence` rows, and `cancel_orphaned_cadences()` sweeps orphans on boot.

In **solo mode** (one person using Open Executive just for themselves; see Org) there are no department check-ins: `bootstrap_cadences()` is a no-op, switching to solo cancels every pending `dept_cadence` row, a row that was already pending is marked `cancelled` by the runner without running and without chaining — ahead of the authority gate, so a `propose_only` department cannot turn it into an approval card, and cancelled rather than done because the nudge engine reads a done check-in as a recent department pulse — and a check-in already running across the switch finishes without `enqueue_next` scheduling another. Switching back to team re-bootstraps them. Solo has one kind of its own, the **weekly review** (`principal_weekly_review`, below): switching to solo seeds it (`seed_weekly_review`), switching to team cancels its pending row (`cancel_weekly_reviews`), and one that fires while the stored mode is team is marked `cancelled` without running or chaining. That check reads the mode strictly (`workspace_settings.read_stored_mode`) and fails open: a mode that can't be read (a locked database) is not taken for team, so one bad read neither retires the review nor breaks its chain — the next run checks again.

The parser also takes a zone: `_parse_cadence_spec(spec, after, tz=UTC)` builds the wall-clock time in `tz` and only then converts to UTC, so a local schedule stays at the same local time across daylight-saving changes (a time the spring-forward gap skips fires once, just after the jump; a time the fall-back repeats fires at its first occurrence).

### The principal's rhythm

The morning brief (`principal_brief_morning`, 08:00), end-of-day digest (`principal_brief_eod`, 18:00) and reflection (`executive_reflection`, 07:30) are seeded once per database by `seed_principal_briefs()` and each chains its next occurrence when it fires. In a solo workspace it also seeds the **weekly review** (`principal_weekly_review`, Friday 16:00 local by default), which runs the `weekly_review` workflow and is delivered like the briefs; its `PRINCIPAL_WEEKLY_REVIEW_TIME` takes a whole weekly spec (`weekly@fri@16:00`), read as UTC when valid, like the pinned times below, and it chains only while the workspace is still solo — and never when a weekly row is already pending, so a switch to solo while a review finishes cannot leave two. Their default times are local to the user's zone — `memory.workspace_settings.get_user_timezone()`: the zone set through `PUT /workspace`, else `USER_TIMEZONE`, else UTC — computed with the cadence parser above. An operator who pinned a valid `HH:MM` in `PRINCIPAL_BRIEF_MORNING_TIME` / `PRINCIPAL_BRIEF_EOD_TIME` / `PRINCIPAL_REFLECTION_TIME` keeps that time read as UTC, as before zones existed, so a pinned time never moves; a malformed value is logged and treated as unset. An install that set `USER_TIMEZONE` but pinned nothing does move to that zone, from each kind's first fire after the upgrade (a row seeded before it keeps its old UTC time once). When the zone in effect changes, `reschedule_principal_rhythm()` re-times each kind's pending, not-yet-due row **in place** — it only updates `run_at` (guarded on the row being unchanged since it was read), never inserts or cancels, so it cannot race a chain into a duplicate. The new time is the next occurrence in the new zone after `max(now, last fired run + 12h)`, so a kind never runs twice within 12 hours; and if that is more than 12 hours later than the row's current time — moving would skip a day, as when someone switches to Europe/London at 07:59 UTC with the 08:00 UTC brief a minute away — the row keeps its time once. A kind with no such row is left alone: a row that is running, one between being marked done and its chain insert, or a due row held by a pause or a missing company profile. Its chain times the next one in the new zone, and the chain itself starts from `max(now, fired run + 12h)`, so a zone change while a brief runs cannot put a second brief a few hours after it. The weekly review follows the same rules with a 3.5-day gap (`_min_gap`) in place of 12 hours, so a zone change can neither run it twice in a week nor skip one.

User-created (dynamic) workflows can carry the same cadence DSL. A cadence-enabled definition enqueues a `dynamic_workflow` action (`workflows.dynamic_cadence`); when due, the runner runs the stored `DynamicWorkflow`, DMs the definition's `cadence_person_id` what the run came to (`workflows/run_message`: a fast-model message written from the full report for its reader — what came of the run in their timezone, no tool or step names — or no message at all when the run found nothing and did nothing they need to hear about; the full report stays on the run), and re-chains the next occurrence. A workflow that reads its creator's own mail or calendar (`delegation.workflow_reads`) runs as theirs instead: the run is created with them as its owner (their history alone), its steps run as them, every audit row is theirs (`private_run`), and the artifact, a held-writes pause's eventual delivery and a failure card go to them whatever the cadence names. Saving/updating/deleting the definition reconciles its pending `dynamic_workflow` rows. A cadence definition may not contain an approval gate — a cron fire has no human to ask — with one exception, the **held-writes** pause: when an action step holds a write to a new target, the runner checkpoints the run (`checkpoint_gate`, the owner is DMed), still marks the row done and re-chains the cadence, and stamps `deliver_to_person_id` on the resume payload so the resumer sends that same message to the cadence recipient once the owner answers (or the 48 h timeout skips the held writes). Any other gate is still refused at execution: it calls `workflows.gate.ensure_workflow_event`, which raises on a gate so the run is recorded as failed. It previously ignored the gate and stored a completed run with `"(no artifact)"` as its body, which looked like a success every period.

**Monthly tally.** On the first weekday of each month, in daytime (09:00–18:00 local), a tick hook beside the reminders (`_maybe_send_monthly_value` → `briefing.value_summary.maybe_send_monthly`, checked every 15 minutes) sends the owner last month's counted lines and a link to Pulse → Your month through `_deliver_to_principal`, in solo and team mode alike. It is claimed once per month (`briefing_narrative` scope `value_summary:YYYY-MM`, never released, so one try), skipped for an empty month, audited `value_summary_sent` / `value_summary_not_sent`, and off with `VALUE_SUMMARY_MONTHLY_ENABLED=false`. It is not a `scheduled_actions` row.

### Department authority & cancelling

A department-scoped row passes the authority gate (`departments.authority.gate_action`, see Org) before it is dispatched: `auto_execute` dispatches; `propose_only` raises an approval card and marks the row done without dispatching (deferred to the approver's next availability window when they are outside it); `escalate` raises an urgent `[ESCALATION]` card (severity high) straight away — never deferred — and likewise does not dispatch, because approving the card is what sends it. As that card is the action's only trace it always lands: unrouted when there is no approver and no principal, and deduped on the whole action (kind, channel, recipient and intent) rather than the summary's first 60 characters, so another escalation sharing an opening — or the same text for someone else — cannot swallow it. An identical escalation folds into a still-open card and gets a fresh one once that card was handled, and a card that cannot be written retries the row with backoff and, once the retries are spent, marks it `failed` — never `done`. (It used to raise the card *and* dispatch.) The runner records which action each card holds (`alert_held_actions`, server-side only, never a tag a model could write): approving one (`POST /alerts/{id}/approve`) queues a copy of that exact action with no department, so it goes out on the next tick without meeting the gate again. A `dept_cadence` row is not gated at all — gating it turned every check-in on a propose-only department (all eight seeded ones) into a one-shot card, and the row never chained its next occurrence. Nudge-engine rows carry no department and bypass the gate.

A `pending` row can be cancelled with `DELETE /scheduled/{id}` — the Pulse page's Cancel; the update only moves a row that is still `pending`, so one the scheduler has just claimed is never overwritten. Cancelling only stops work, so, like pause, any signed-in user may: the route accepts a signed-in caller through the UI proxy (its `x-caller-email`, trusted only alongside the `BACKEND_SHARED_SECRET` `x-api-key`), a matching `X-Admin-Token` (`SCHEDULED_ADMIN_TOKEN`, for scripts), or a loopback caller when no token is set — otherwise 401 (token set) or 503. Each cancel is audited as `scheduled_action_cancelled` with who did it.

### Channel routing & nudges

The delivery channel lives on the `scheduled_actions` row (`channel` / `channel_ref`); the runner dispatches through whichever was set at enqueue time — `telegram`, `slack_dm`, `discord_dm`, `email`, or `__internal__` (workflow steps and heartbeats bypass outbound dispatch). Rows left pending by the removed staff-onboarding kinds drain through that same `__internal__` short-circuit (marked done, no dispatch); the removed talent workflows' *ad-hoc* reminders sat on the principal's real DM channel instead, so a one-shot startup sweep (`memory.episodic.cancel_orphaned_talent_reminders`) cancels them — `ad_hoc`, no department, `pending` or `running`, matching the five generated reminder shapes (outreach, interview coordination, reference checks, onboarding check-in, offer expiry) — and clears the awaiting-reply flag on delivered ones so the nudge engine stops chasing them. The marker row in `app_migrations` is claimed first with `INSERT OR IGNORE` in the same transaction, so concurrent boots cannot double-run or crash. The nudge engine (`scheduler.nudge_engine`, default 15 min) scans stalled `awaiting_human` runs, stale commitments, and idle initiatives, then emits `proactive_nudge` rows routed via `people.channel.prefer_channel_for` — honouring each Person's preferred (last-used) channel and availability windows, deferring those outside their window and skipping those with no reachable channel. Emission is capped per `scope_key` (`NUDGE_MAX_PER_SCOPE`, default 3 delivered nudges) so a parked item is not chased forever.

An idle initiative is chased with its department's head; with no head to resolve — no department (what the episodic extractor stores), an unknown department, or no head set — the principal owns it. That source used to skip every initiative without a head, so in practice it never fired. The principal gets self-addressed wording ("<title>" has not moved since <date> — still active, done, or dropped?). If channel routing cannot reach the principal (no channel configured, or unreachable beyond `NUDGE_MAX_DEFER_DAYS`), the nudge becomes an unrouted Briefing card instead, keyed on the initiative and the ISO week: at most one card per initiative per week, and while one is still unread the scan leaves it alone rather than refreshing it every 15 minutes. The emitted nudge still carries no department, and the usual caps and cooldowns apply. A department-tagged initiative is still skipped while its department's check-in actually ran inside the idle window; a skipped check-in does not count.

The stale-commitment source also chases **open loops** (see Attunement): `scheduled_actions` rows with `kind='open_loop'`, recorded `done` on the `__internal__` channel so the runner never dispatches them, whose `awaiting_response_since` is the loop's *due time*. They are chased as soon as they are overdue — not after `NUDGE_COMMITMENT_STALE_DAYS` — with a check-in intent addressed to the loop's owner (which quotes only the owner's own verbatim words and tells the dispatching turn to treat them as data), through the same `prefer_channel_for` routing, availability windows and outbound guard. Until open loops existed nothing in production set `awaiting_response_since`, so this source had nothing to chase. Each scan first closes loops older than `ATTUNEMENT_LOOP_TTL_DAYS` (21) as `expired`, then marks proactive outreach nobody answered within `ATTUNEMENT_IGNORE_AFTER_HOURS` as `ignored` in the outcome ledger. Ranking uses that ledger: a candidate whose person left their last five resolved nudges of that kind unanswered ranks after all others and waits three times its cooldown; a single answer lifts it. Approving a stalled run (however it's approved) and updating an initiative count as acting on the nudges that chased them. The generic dispatch path tags each send with its source (`_outreach_source`) so the ledger can attribute it.

### Alert lifecycle: expiry sweep and the review heartbeat

Two alert-maintenance jobs live here. The **expiry sweep** is loop-level, not a heartbeat row: `_maybe_sweep_alerts` runs `alerts.lifecycle.expire_stale_alerts` (and, on the same 15-minute throttle, `monitoring.research.watch_policy.sweep` — expiring unreviewed research watch suggestions, auto-disabling research-added watches that proved noisy or dead, and filing one `watchlist_suggestions` nudge when ≥3 suggestions have waited ≥7 days; see External monitoring) once at boot and every 15 minutes at the top of the tick — before the company-profile and rotation gates, so an old backlog expires even before onboarding completes, flipping `unread` alerts past their category TTL to `expired` and auditing `alert_sweep`. Pure DB hygiene, no model call, reversible via `POST /alerts/{id}/reopen`. The same throttled call also deletes Always in the loop notes past their expiry (`memory.history.sweep_expired`; reads already skip them, and it never raises). Each tick also calls `_maybe_remind_notes` → `memory.history_reminders.maybe_remind` (its own 15-minute throttle, 09:00–18:00 local, one task at a time): a person whose notes say something they promised by email is due today gets one message saying how many, through `deliver_to_person` — the brief's own channel order for any Person, never a shared channel (`delivery_order` now skips a Telegram group id, for the briefs too); a message `_send_on_plan` sends into a Telegram chat or Slack or Discord DM is saved into that chat's current conversation (`integrations.conversations.record_delivery`, see Integrations), so a reply to a brief, digest or report has it in view, with the senders' audit rows private to that person. A hook rather than a `scheduled_actions` row, which `/scheduled` would show to everyone (see Memory).

The **Executive alert review** is a real heartbeat — kind `alert_review_scan`, `__internal__` channel, bootstrapped idempotently at startup when `ALERT_REVIEW_ENABLED` and chained every `ALERT_REVIEW_INTERVAL_HOURS` (6) with the same crash-resilient run → mark-done → chain shape as `nudge_scan`. `_run_principal_brief` also runs a `pre_brief` pass right before the morning brief (a review failure never blocks the brief). Each pass re-examines open alerts with evidence and, within department authority and the privacy rule, routes, nudges, escalates, drafts, merges or resolves them — see the Today section for the policy. The moves go through the real handlers (`message_person`, `draft_artifact`), so the outbound anti-spam guard applies, and `ALERT_REVIEW_MAX_MOVES_PER_SCAN` bounds side effects per pass.

The /today **"What's going on" header** is kept current from the tick too, so it is fresh before anyone opens the page. `_maybe_refresh_narrative` is a throttled call inside the loop, like the alert sweep — no `scheduled_actions` row. It runs after the pause, company-profile and rotation gates, every `BRIEFING_NARRATIVE_REFRESH_MINUTES` (10; 0 turns it off) and only between `BRIEFING_NARRATIVE_REFRESH_START_HOUR` and `_END_HOUR` (06–22) in the user's zone. It starts `today.refresh_principal_narrative` as its own task, so a slow model call never holds the tick, and never starts a second while one runs. That refreshes the cached calendar read (`live_signals.refresh_calendar`, at most once per 15 minutes) and rewrites the principal's header only when its key moved — new mail, a held reply, a proposal, the hour — with the route's own per-scope lock, so a page view and the tick never write the same header twice (see Today).

Act as me's **reminders** are loop-level too: `_maybe_send_reminders` starts `delegation.reminders.maybe_send` at most once a minute, which claims each due `delegation_reminders` row once (due times are stored in UTC, so they compare in order) (compare-and-set on `claimed_at`) and sends its stored text, prefixed "Reminder you set on <date>:", to the person who set it alone through `deliver_to_person`. No model and no tool run; a reminder missed by more than two days is dropped rather than sent late, and one due in the person's quiet hours or leave waits, unclaimed, until they end; audit rows are private to the person. They are not `scheduled_actions` rows for the same reason as the scan below: that list is everyone's, and its rows run an Executive turn when they fire.

**Held messages** are loop-level as well: `_maybe_release_held` starts `people.held_messages.maybe_release` at most once a minute, which sends each person whatever is due to them — messages held for their quiet hours once those end, and brief-held messages made due when the briefs run — as one *While you were away* message through `deliver_to_person`, claims each row first so a brief can't send it too, marks them sent only once that went, postpones a person back in quiet hours, on leave or outside their windows to when that ends, backs off 2, 4, 8 … minutes (at most an hour) after any other failure, and audits every drop (too old, over the cap) privately as a count, and writes audit rows private to the person. The principal-brief handler appends the principal's brief-held messages to the morning brief or end-of-day digest it delivers (`_with_held_messages`; the stored run artifact is unchanged), claims them, marks them sent only when the brief went (otherwise frees the claim), then makes everyone else's due (`_release_others_digests`). The `proactive_nudge` re-check calls `prefer_channel_for` / `next_available_window` with `quiet_hours=True` (urgent for a `nudge:stalled:` scope key), so a nudge due in the person's quiet hours is deferred to their end like one outside an availability window. A dispatch whose message was held is audited `held`, not `delivered`. See Org for the notification settings.

Act as me's **inbox watcher** is loop-level the same way: `_maybe_scan_inbox`, after the same gates, starts the due scans (`delegation.inbox.maybe_scan`) as one task and never a second while one runs. A person is due every `DELEGATION_INBOX_POLL_MINUTES` (default 5) once their **Draft replies to my inbox** switch is on, unless a Gmail failure set a back-off; nobody is scanned while a client slot is active. It is deliberately not a `scheduled_actions` row: those are listed on `/scheduled` for everyone and anyone may cancel them, and a scan reads the owner's own mail. Every row a scan writes is private to the principal (see Act as Me).

The **contact keeper** is loop-level too: `_maybe_keep_contacts`, right after the inbox watcher, calls `people.contact_keeper.maybe_run`, which starts one pass at most every 6 hours (an in-process start time plus the stored `last_run_at`, so a restart doesn't re-run it) and never a second while one runs. Like the scans it is not a `scheduled_actions` row, because it reads the principal's own mail. See Org.

### Principal briefs

The `principal_brief_morning` / `principal_brief_eod` / `principal_weekly_review` rows (and the client-rotation digest) are delivered by `_deliver_to_principal`, not through a row channel. The principal's `preferred_channel` (`slack` / `discord` / `telegram` / `email` / `any`, where `any` means the chat app they last talked in) is tried first, then the other chat channels they have an id for (Slack → Discord → Telegram), by `people.reach.reach_order`. Email goes through the active MCP gateway: first when the preference is `email`, and otherwise last, as the backup after every chat channel. Before planning, the delivery asks the gateway supervisor for a start if the gateway is down (`runner.ensure_email_ready` → `mcp_gateway.ensure_active_gateway`, the lazy re-check), and a row action resolves the gateway at execution time rather than from what boot had, so a gateway that failed at boot and came up on a retry carries the brief. The outcome names what happened: `gateway_down` when email is set up but the gateway is not running (the Executive's fault, with the start failure, never `no_channel`, which blamed the owner's setup), and a `send_failed` detail that quotes each channel's own error (`email: invalid_grant …`, `slack_dm: channel_not_found`), stored with the outcome (`brief_state.record_delivery_outcome(detail=…)`) and shown on the Briefing notice and the Setup page's *Daily brief* light, whose fix says to reconnect when the detail shows a dead grant. Delivery stops at the first channel that sends, so an owner linked by email at setup keeps their Slack delivery without extra email, and gets the brief by email only when Slack is missing or fails. The email is formatted HTML (`utils.markdown_email`: raw HTML and images off, unsafe link schemes dropped) with a subject dated in the user's zone ("Morning Brief — Fri 25 Sep"). Email counts as ready only when the MCP gateway runs the Google Workspace server. Every run's outcome — delivered, no owner, nowhere to send it, every send failed, or the brief couldn't be written at all (the workflow failed or produced nothing) — is recorded with the channel's name (never an address) under `brief_state`, for the Briefing's notice and the Setup status "Daily brief" light (the weekly review's outcome too — `brief_state.DELIVERY_KINDS` — so a weekly review that wasn't sent is reported the same way). The light also turns amber when a brief got through only on a backup channel, naming the one that failed. `_run_principal_brief` sets `morning_brief.PRINCIPAL_DELIVERY` for the run, because it goes to the principal alone: only then (or on the principal's own verified chat turn) does the morning brief read what is private to them. When the workflow reports `private_to_principal` on its `result` event — it did read such a row — the run history keeps `persistence.PRIVATE_RUN_ARTIFACT` in place of the text (`stored_artifact`), since `/workflows/runs` is readable by everyone signed in; the principal gets the full text where it is delivered. When no channel can deliver at all (a web-only principal, or email with no gateway), the brief is still generated and stored as a run with its artifact — a web-only principal reads it on the Artifacts page — it is just not delivered, and the next occurrence is chained; see Workflows.

## Client rotation claim pause

The `client_rotation` kind (multi-client practice mode, opt-in via `CLIENT_ROTATION_ENABLED`) adds one loop-level behavior: while a rotation's `.rotation_in_progress` marker exists, the scheduler **skips claiming entirely** for that tick. Rotation switches the live company context between parked clients; claiming during the window would fire the just-activated client's overdue outbound follow-ups from a context nobody is watching. Everything due fires on the first tick after the original client is restored. Stale markers (crash mid-rotation) are reconciled at scheduler startup, and the rotation row is idempotently re-seeded both at boot and after every slot activation (scheduled rows swap with the client). See the Client Companies section for the rotation's full design.

An optional `notion_sync_scan` heartbeat (`NOTION_SYNC_ENABLED`, off by default) incrementally re-indexes Notion pages the workspace integration can see into the isolated `notion_wiki` collection (not COMPANY), reconciles un-shared pages, then chains the next tick. An optional `drive_sync_scan` heartbeat (`DRIVE_SYNC_ENABLED`, off by default, bootstrapped in the lifespan beside it) does the same for the configured Google Drive folders, into the isolated `drive_docs` collection (see RAG). An optional `onedrive_sync_scan` heartbeat (`ONEDRIVE_SYNC_ENABLED`, off by default) does the same for the configured OneDrive folders, into `onedrive_docs`. An optional `confluence_sync_scan` heartbeat (`CONFLUENCE_SYNC_ENABLED`, off by default, bootstrapped in the lifespan the same way) re-indexes the changed pages of the configured Confluence spaces into the isolated `confluence_wiki` collection, leaving out restricted pages, and purges pages that were deleted, moved out or restricted.

**Take the lead wakes.** With Take the lead as the Executive on, a turn from a channel (mail, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Google Chat) calls `take_the_lead.wake`, which inserts one `take_the_lead_wake` `__internal__` action five minutes out. It does nothing while one is pending or running, and nothing within 30 minutes of the last wake. The runner's `_run_take_the_lead_wake` runs the same reflection as the daily rhythm (`_reflect`, shared with `_run_executive_reflection`), only if the switch is still on, and never chains. The pause holds it like every claim.

**Conversation reviews.** A kept chat turn (`memory.chat_review.record_turn`) makes sure one `chat_review` `__internal__` action is waiting for that conversation (`channel_ref` = session id), 30 minutes (`CHAT_REVIEW_QUIET_MINUTES`) out. `_run_chat_review` marks it done, then `chat_review.run_scheduled` either schedules a fresh one for 30 minutes after the newest turn (the chat is still going) or reviews the turns not yet reviewed. It never chains, and the pause holds it like every claim.

**Replay of the misses.** The `chat_replay` kind (`memory.replay`) is seeded with the briefs by `seed_principal_briefs()` and chains its next occurrence like the reflection (`_run_chat_replay`; `CHAT_REPLAY_TIME`, 03:30 in the user's zone, pinned as UTC when set). It replays the turns the conversation review graded a miss with the lessons and facts in force today, in a dry run, judges each, and records the night (`chat_review_replay_runs`) whether or not anything was due; a failed night still marks done and chains. The pause holds it like every claim.
